notice: An educational starting point, not a declaration of religious identity. Reference profiles are summaries of the linked sources, not endorsements by those churches. Local information is only confirmed when published by a church representative.

dimensions.title: God and the Trinity
dimensions.question: Which understanding of God is closest to your belief?
dimensions.explanation: These statements describe different understandings of God, not how strongly someone believes.

options.label: One God in three distinct persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit
Father, Son and Holy Ghost are distinct beings united in purpose
One God revealed as Father, Son and Holy Spirit, rather than three distinct persons

dimensions.title: Scripture
dimensions.question: Which description of Scripture is closest to your belief?
dimensions.explanation: This asks about the place of Scripture. The next question asks who interprets it authoritatively.

options.label: The Bible is the uniquely authoritative written Scripture
Other revealed books are Scripture alongside the Bible

dimensions.title: Teaching authority
dimensions.question: How should the church resolve questions of Christian teaching?
dimensions.explanation: All these approaches value Scripture; they differ over the authority of tradition and church teaching.

options.label: Scripture is the final authority over church traditions
Scripture is understood within authoritative apostolic tradition
Scripture and apostolic tradition are interpreted by the teaching office in communion with the pope
Scripture and continuing revelation through living prophets

sources.title: The Orthodox Faith — Orthodox Church in America

dimensions.title: Who is baptized
dimensions.question: Who should receive baptism?
dimensions.explanation: Infant baptism and baptism after a personal profession of faith express different understandings of initiation.

options.label: People who personally profess faith
Infants as well as people who personally profess faith

dimensions.title: Meaning of baptism
dimensions.question: What do you believe baptism does?
dimensions.explanation: The word symbol does not always mean merely symbolic. Choose the statement closest to your understanding.

options.label: An act of obedience and public testimony to faith
A means through which God gives grace and brings us into new life
A sign and seal of God’s covenant, received within the community

dimensions.title: How baptism is administered
dimensions.question: Which forms of baptism would you accept?
dimensions.explanation: This is separate from who is baptized or what baptism means.

options.label: Immersion only
Immersion, pouring or sprinkling

sources.title: The Episcopal Church: What We Believe

dimensions.title: Meaning of Communion
dimensions.question: Which description of Communion is closest to your belief?
dimensions.explanation: Eucharist, Communion and Lord’s Supper name the same central Christian meal. These choices summarize distinct teachings; explanations matter.

options.label: A memorial meal symbolizing Christ’s death
A real participation in Christ through the Holy Spirit
The bread and wine truly become Christ’s body and blood, received as a mystery
The substance of bread and wine becomes Christ’s body and blood
Christ’s body and blood are truly present with the bread and wine

sources.title: The Orthodox Faith — Orthodox Church in America

dimensions.title: Spiritual gifts
dimensions.question: How do you understand gifts such as prophecy, tongues and healing today?
dimensions.explanation: Believing that gifts continue does not necessarily mean expecting them at every service.

options.label: These gifts can continue today
The apostolic sign gifts are no longer ordinarily given

dimensions.title: Spirit baptism and tongues
dimensions.question: Must baptism in the Holy Spirit initially be evidenced by speaking in tongues?
dimensions.explanation: This is more specific than whether someone believes tongues can occur.

options.label: Yes
No

dimensions.title: Church leadership
dimensions.question: Which form of church leadership do you seek?
dimensions.explanation: Local leadership and wider church authority are related but distinct from worship style.

options.label: An autonomous congregation
Elders and regional assemblies
Bishops in apostolic succession
Bishops in communion with the pope
A connected church with shared regional oversight

sources.title: The Orthodox Faith — Orthodox Church in America

dimensions.title: Intercession of saints
dimensions.question: Would you affirm asking departed saints to pray for us?
dimensions.explanation: Catholic and Orthodox teaching distinguishes asking for intercession from worship of God.

options.label: Yes
No

sources.title: The Orthodox Faith — Orthodox Church in America

dimensions.title: Confession
dimensions.question: What place should confession to a priest have?
dimensions.explanation: This asks about sacramental confession, not whether Christians should admit wrongdoing or seek counsel.

options.label: It should be available as a sacramental practice
Confession to God does not require a priestly sacrament

sources.title: The Orthodox Faith — Orthodox Church in America

dimensions.title: Sabbath observance
dimensions.question: Is observance of the seventh-day Sabbath binding for Christians?
dimensions.explanation: This concerns belief about Sabbath, not which day is convenient to attend.

options.label: Yes, the seventh-day Sabbath should be observed
No, Christians may gather on Sunday without that requirement

dimensions.title: Grace and faith
dimensions.question: Which statement best describes your understanding of salvation?
dimensions.explanation: These are brief summaries, not a test of devotion. All listed Christian traditions speak of God’s grace; their accounts differ.

options.label: Justification is by grace through faith alone; good works follow as its fruit
Salvation is by grace, lived through faith, love and participation in the life of Christ

sources.title: The Orthodox Faith — Orthodox Church in America

dimensions.title: Pattern of worship
dimensions.question: What pattern of worship would you seek?
dimensions.explanation: A congregation may offer different services. This preference does not determine its doctrine.

options.label: A structured historic liturgy
A flexible service centered on preaching and prayer
I would enjoy either

sources.title: The Episcopal Church: What We Believe

dimensions.title: Communion frequency
dimensions.question: How often would you like Communion to be offered?
dimensions.explanation: Local schedules must be confirmed by the congregation.

options.label: Weekly or more
Approximately monthly
Less often

sources.title: The Orthodox Faith — Orthodox Church in America

dimensions.title: Rosary
dimensions.question: How would you feel about a church regularly offering rosary?
dimensions.explanation: A prayer practice reflecting on the life of Christ with Marian prayers.

options.label: I would seek this out
I am comfortable with it
I would prefer a church without this organized practice

dimensions.title: Eucharistic adoration
dimensions.question: How would you feel about a church regularly offering eucharistic adoration?
dimensions.explanation: Prayer before the consecrated Eucharist outside the main service.

options.label: I would seek this out
I am comfortable with it
I would prefer a church without this organized practice

dimensions.title: Veneration of icons
dimensions.question: How would you feel about a church regularly offering veneration of icons?
dimensions.explanation: Showing honor through sacred images, distinguished from worship of God.

options.label: I would seek this out
I am comfortable with it
I would prefer a church without this organized practice

sources.title: The Orthodox Faith — Orthodox Church in America

dimensions.explanation: Regular shared prayer, including a daily office or other prayer gatherings.

dimensions.explanation: Reading and discussing Scripture together.

dimensions.explanation: A community rhythm of fasting, with pastoral accommodations.

dimensions.explanation: Small gatherings for shared prayer and mutual support.

dimensions.question: How would you feel about a church regularly offering works of mercy?
dimensions.explanation: Organized opportunities to serve neighbors and people in need.

I am comfortable with it
I would prefer a church without this organized practice

traditions.name: Catholic
traditions.summary: Explore sacramental life, apostolic tradition and communion with the pope. Local devotions and schedules need parish confirmation.

traditions.name: Eastern Orthodox — OCA reference
traditions.summary: An introduction through Orthodox Church in America teaching. Other Orthodox jurisdictions and local practices should be explored directly.

sources.title: The Orthodox Faith — Orthodox Church in America

traditions.name: Southern Baptist
traditions.summary: A reference based on the Baptist Faith and Message. Congregations are autonomous; confirm local statements and practices.

traditions.name: Lutheran — Missouri Synod
traditions.summary: A reference for the LCMS specifically, not a profile of all Lutheran churches.

traditions.name: United Methodist
traditions.summary: Explore grace, baptism and a connected community. Local congregations should confirm practices and participation guidance.

traditions.name: Presbyterian Church (USA)
traditions.summary: A limited reference to Presbyterian sacramental teaching; other Presbyterian bodies may differ.

traditions.name: The Episcopal Church
traditions.summary: Explore a tradition shaped by Scripture and the Book of Common Prayer. Congregational expression varies.

sources.title: The Episcopal Church: What We Believe

traditions.name: Assemblies of God (USA)
traditions.summary: A Pentecostal reference based on the denomination’s Fundamental Truths; it does not stand for all Pentecostal churches.

traditions.name: Seventh-day Adventist
traditions.summary: Explore the denomination’s official fundamental beliefs, including seventh-day Sabbath observance.

traditions.name: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
traditions.summary: Included consistently with the directory. Its account of the Godhead and continuing revelation differs from Nicene Trinitarian traditions.
